job_title: Strategic Website Designer, Figma + Website Strategy
description: Full-Time Remote Role, Philippines-Based ---------------------------------------------------------- We are looking for a full-time Strategic Website Designer based in the Philippines. This role is ideal for someone who is strong in Figma, understands website design, and can think strategically about clients, their customers, brand direction, industry patterns, and what makes a website work. This is not just a production design role. We are looking for someone who can understand the brief, think through the customer journey, research competitors, recommend website direction, and then support that direction in Figma. Role Overview ------------------- You will help turn client goals, customer needs, brand direction, website references, and competitor research into a clear internal website strategy and design direction. You do not need to lead client calls, but you must be able to sit in meetings, understand what clients are saying, extract the important points, and translate that into useful internal notes, design direction, and Figma updates. You will work closely with our internal team across website strategy, design, and delivery Key Responsibilities --------------------------- - Review client briefs, meeting notes, recordings, brand assets, and website references - Understand what the client wants, what their customers need, and what the website needs to achieve - Analyse websites the client likes and dislikes - Research competitor websites and industry patterns - Identify trust signals, conversion sections, content structure, and visual styles that work in each industry - Recommend website direction based on customer needs and business goals - Create look-and-feel concepts in Figma - Create new website sections in Figma - Improve layout, spacing, hierarchy, flow, and visual polish - Update existing Figma designs based on internal direction - Write clear internal notes explaining design decisions and strategic recommendations - Keep ClickUp tasks updated with progress, blockers, and time entries - Communicate clearly with the team via Slack and Google Docs - Use ChatGPT to support research, summaries, and strategic thinking where useful What We Are Looking For ----------------------------------- You should be a mid-to-senior-level website designer with strong strategic thinking. You should be able to take messy input and turn it into clear website direction. We are looking for someone who can think before designing. A strong candidate can say: “Based on the customer’s needs, the homepage should build trust early, show proof, and make the offer clear, reduce friction, and use a more premium visual direction because the market is crowded.” A weak candidate only says: “I can make modern websites in Figma.” We are looking for the first type. Required Skills --------------------- - Strong Figma skills - Website design experience - Ability to create new website sections, not just edit existing designs - Good understanding of layout, spacing, hierarchy, and visual polish - Ability to create early look-and-feel concepts - Ability to understand client brands - Ability to analyse competitor websites - Ability to understand customer needs and website goals - Clear written English for internal notes and design rationale - Good communication in Slack and Google Docs - Comfortable using ClickUp for task updates and time tracking - Comfortable using ChatGPT as a thinking and research support tool English Requirement ----------------------------- You do not need to be a copywriter or client presenter. However, you must be able to write clear internal notes, summarise client requirements, explain design decisions, and provide simple website section direction. Example of the level we need: “The client wants the site to feel modern, premium, and trustworthy. Their customers are likely comparing providers, so the homepage should quickly communicate credibility, outcomes, and service clarity. The reference websites suggest they prefer clean layouts, strong imagery, and simple navigation.” Tools You Must Be Comfortable With ---------------------------------------------------- - Figma - ClickUp - Slack - Google Docs - ChatGPT Work Hours ----------------- This is a full-time role. You must be available to work: - 9:00 am to 5:30 pm Australian Eastern Standard Time For candidates in the Philippines, this is usually around: - 7:00 am to 3:30 pm Philippines time Please only apply if you can work these hours long-term. Role Structure ------------------- - Full-time remote contractor role - Philippines-based candidates only - 3-month probation period - If successful after probation, the role continues on the same agreed monthly salary - 1 week notice during probation - 2 weeks' notice after probation - Unpaid leave only - Contractor must provide their own laptop, stable internet, and suitable work setup - This is a fully exclusive role. You must not work with other clients while engaged in this role - Daily time tracking is required in ClickUp - No screenshots or activity monitoring required - Confidentiality and IP ownership agreement required Access and Confidentiality ------------------------------------ You will have access to internal documentation, project files, client information, Figma files, brand assets, and other materials required to do the role well. All work created during the role, including strategy notes, design concepts, Figma files, website layouts, written documentation, research outputs, and related assets, will be owned by the company. You may not share client work publicly, use it in a portfolio, or reuse it elsewhere without written approval. Who This Role Is Not For --------------------------------- Please do not apply if: - You only want to follow the exact design instructions - You are not comfortable thinking strategically - You cannot explain your design decisions - You do not like researching competitors or industries - You only want production design tasks - You cannot work 9:00 am to 5:30 pm AEST - You are currently working with other clients and want to keep doing so - You are not comfortable with ClickUp time tracking How To Apply -------------------- Submit your application to ---------- Please include the following in your application: 1. A short introduction about yourself 2. Your Figma portfolio or links to website design work 3. Your expected monthly salary in PHP 4. Confirmation that you can work 9:00 am to 5:30 pm AEST 5. Confirmation that you are available for a full-time exclusive role 6. A short answer to this question: “Tell us about a website you designed or improved. What was the client trying to achieve, and who was the customer, and why did you choose that design direction?” Applications that only say “I am interested” without answering the above will not be considered

title: Full-Time Graphic Designer & Social Video Content Creator
job_title: Full-Time Graphic Designer & Social Video Content Creator
description: About Us Reputation Elevation provides a full suite of digital marketing services, with a special focus on the autism therapy (ABA) space. Innovation, exceptional client service, and real results are at our core. Our design team produces a high volume of paid-social and Google ad creative — fast, on-brand, and built to perform. The Role We’re hiring a full-time Graphic Designer and Social Media Video Creator with genuine taste and creative instinct. You have a sharp eye for design, you can write a headline that stops the scroll, and you can turn a brief into polished image and video ads quickly. You’ll work closely with our ads team to concept and produce creative that wins attention and drives leads. This is a high-output, direct-response role. You’ll often work within strict brand and content constraints (more on that below) and still find a way to make the work feel fresh. If you love the craft of making one ad clearly outperform another, you’ll fit in here. Creativity is only half the job. The other half is execution: being quick, organized, and meticulous. A typical assignment is a set of graphics and short videos due in 3 business days — and “due in 3 business days” means done in 3 business days. Many clients run campaigns in multiple cities, so you’ll often produce near-identical creative sets that differ only in the details — the Atlanta set says Atlanta, the Savannah set says Savannah, and every location-specific element is right in each one. If that level of precision sounds tedious, this isn’t the role; if it sounds obvious, read on. What You’ll Do • Concept and produce high-quality image and video ads for Facebook /Instagram and Google. • Write short, punchy on-asset copy and headlines — not just lay out design. • Tailor creative to ABA therapy providers and our other client industries. • Localize creative sets for multi-market clients — same campaign, different city — getting every location-specific detail right on every version. • Use generative AI as a core part of your workflow to move fast without sacrificing taste. • Partner with the ads team to understand each client and ship creative that hits the campaign goal. • Turn work around on schedule — a standard set of graphics and short videos is assigned with a 3-business-day deadline, and it ships on time, every time. • Deliver organized, editable source files for everything you make. • Keep current on what’s working in paid-social creative and bring ideas to the table. Tools You’ll Use We care about output and taste more than any specific software, but you should be fluent across these categories: • Canva — core to our workflow; you should be very comfortable here. • AI video generation — comfort with current AI video tools for generating and animating ad footage. • Image editing — a professional editor such as Photoshop (or equivalent). • AI image generation — generating and refining on-brand still imagery. • Video editing — assembling short-form video with text, captions, and music. How We Work • Schedule — Full-time. You set your own hours, but you must be reliably available for live overlap from 3:00–6:00 PM Israel time for calls and feedback. • Deadlines — A typical assignment is a set of graphics and short videos with a 3-business-day turnaround. Deadlines are firm; if something threatens one, you flag it early, not on the due date. • Project management — Assignments are managed in ClickUp. • File handling — All work, including editable source files, is uploaded to our shared Google Drive. • Ad accounts — You may be added to our clients’ Facebook Ads accounts to upload creative. Content Standards (Please Read) Our ABA therapy clients require brand-safe, conservative creative. The first rule applies to every asset; the depiction rules apply whenever people appear: • The word “autism” or “ABA therapy” must be clearly visible in the text of every ad. • When people are shown, they’re conservatively dressed — elbows, knees, and collarbones covered — with conservative hairstyles. • Any children depicted read as ordinary, neurotypical kids. • When therapists are shown, they wear casual professional clothing — no lab coats or scrubs. If tightly constrained creative frustrates you, this likely isn’t the right role. If you see constraints as a fun problem to solve, you’ll thrive. We only view job applications from people who really read this through. Prove you read this by including the word “elephant” in your application message. Creative Range (Also Please Read) The rules above govern what appears on an asset — they do not mean every ad shows a therapy session, a child, or even a person. Many of our best-performing creatives don’t. Styles in our rotation include: • Text-only — typographic ads where the headline is the design. • Mood-setting — e.g., aerial footage of a beautiful landscape with a line about autism or ABA written over it. • Animated — animation works when it’s tasteful; it must never read as anime or feel immature. • UGC-style — an image or video of a parent at home, or a therapist working while a parent watches, with text on top. Feels authentic rather than produced. That list isn’t a menu to pick from — it’s a starting point. There are endless creative styles to innovate, and part of this job is bringing us formats we haven’t tried. We want someone who works within our rules and keeps pushing the style range. What We’re Looking For • Proven experience designing paid-social / direct-response ad creative (image and video). Please share a portfolio of ad work specifically — not only brand or editorial pieces. • A strong eye for layout, type, and what makes a scroll-stopping ad. • A style innovator — someone who moves fluently between text-only, mood-driven, animated, and UGC-style formats, and keeps proposing new ones we haven’t tried. • Solid short-form copy/headline instincts. • Real, current experience using generative AI for images and graphics. • Sharp attention to detail — especially across near-duplicate versions of the same creative (different cities, phone numbers, offers) where one wrong detail means a wrong ad goes live. • Organized and dependably on time — you manage multiple clients and deadlines at once, hit a 3-business-day turnaround consistently, and never drop quality to do it. • Clear communicator who collaborates well with a remote team. • Pluses: experience in the ABA therapy / autism space, and the ability to produce high-quality AI-generated video ads. Our Hiring Process Four steps, in this order: 1. Video screener — a short, asynchronous video Q&A via VideoAsk. A few quick questions you answer on camera, on your own schedule. No preparation needed. 2. Portfolio — send a portfolio of paid-social / direct-response ad work (image and video). Given the conservative standards of our client base, portfolios must contain no indecent or risqué imagery — submissions that include it will not be reviewed. 3. Paid test assignment — a small, paid creative brief done to a real deadline, so we can see your taste, your process, and your reliability under our actual working conditions. 4. Interview — a live conversation about your work, your test, and the role. What We Offer • Full-time remote role with flexibility in how you structure your day. • A supportive, collaborative team that ships a lot of work. • Real impact on our clients’ marketing results. • Competitive compensation based on experience and skill. Join us in creating visually stunning, high-performing ad campaigns that make a difference.

description: Hi! I run a Christian faith and wellness brand and I’m looking for a reliable video editor to be my go-to person for short-form content. WHAT I’M LOOKING FOR: • Experience with vertical short-form editing • Fast, consistent, reliable turnaround — this is daily volume • Ability to follow a template/brand style for consistency • Good communication, someone I can count on long-term TO APPLY, PLEASE SEND: 1. A few examples of short-form videos you’ve edited — ideally at least one with a strong hook and zoom-in/zoom-out style 2. Your monthly rate for 4 videos/day 3. Your turnaround time for a batch of videos 4. One sentence on why this kind of faith/wellness content appeals to you I pay every two weeks (biweekly). Organized project structure is not optional Reliable internet, capable hardware, and a professional home edit setup Strong communication. You can take feedback without ego and give feedback with clarity WHAT SETS YOU APART You've worked on short films, brand campaigns, or editorial-grade content, not just listing videos You understand light. You push back when something isn't right You've built motion graphics from scratch, not just dropped in templates You know what good audio design does to a real estate film THE WORK ENVIRONMENT Remote. Async-first. Direct communication with the founder. No corporate layers. No committees. Fast feedback, high standards, and real creative latitude when you've earned the trust. This starts as a project-based engagement. For the right person it grows into a core team role. We are building something with a long shelf life and we want people who want to build it with us. COMPENSATION Project-based or retainer, depending on volume and fit. Rates are competitive and reflect the quality of the work we expect. We don't lowball creatives. Some of it runs organically as shoppable content; some of it runs as paid ads. Either way, good editing is what makes someone stop, watch, and buy. It's a volume game. The more strong content we put out, the more we grow — and when we grow, everyone who helped build it grows too. Your edits don't disappear into a void. Think of every post as a seed: plant enough good ones and they turn into real revenue — for the brand, for the company, and for you. That's the whole point. We win as a team, and we want a teammate who's hungry to win. ________________________________________ What We're Really Looking For (Read This Part Twice) Skills can be taught. Drive can't. Before anything else, we want someone who: •	Is genuinely fired up to make great content — not just clock hours •	Believes they can produce high-quality work. And if you're not fully there yet — that's okay. We will train you. But you have to want it. •	Is coachable — takes feedback without ego and applies it to the very next edit •	Is ready to commit. We pour real time, training, and trust into our editors. So we're looking for someone who will commit back and build something long-term with us — not someone passing through. ________________________________________ What You'll Do •	Edit short-form videos in our brand style •	Turn organized B-roll plans and raw footage into scroll-stopping cuts •	Organizing files in Google Drive using our folder and naming structure •	Collaborate in ---------- for feedback, revisions, and approvals •	Keep your project status updated in Airtable as you work •	Learn our niche and audience — who they are and how they watch •	Follow our documented workflows and creative standards •	Apply feedback and get sharper with every single edit ________________________________________ Who We're Looking For Required •	Female editor (to match our brand and audience) •	Short-form social editing experience •	Strong storytelling instincts •	Organized and detail-oriented •	Reliable communication and availability •	Comfortable working inside a structured, documented system •	Fired up, coachable, and ready to commit (see the section above — this matters most) Huge Plus •	Experience editing for female creators •	Familiar with wellness, fitness, or lifestyle niches •	Experience with affiliate or UGC-style content •	You genuinely enjoy systems, clarity, and repeatable workflows ________________________________________ Compensation We pay hourly, and we keep it simple and fair. How it works •	You're paid for the hours you work. Tell us your preferred hourly rate when you apply. •	Prefer a salary? Once you've proven out, we offer salaried arrangements — and the deal is straightforward: commit to your hours, consistently show up, and we pay your full contracted amount, even on a week you come up a little short. (If hours drop far below what we agreed, pay reflects the hours actually worked. Hit your commitment and you never have to think about it.) Bonuses & extras •	We regularly add bonuses and extra pay onto paychecks for strong work. When you make us look good, we take care of you. •	We run team challenges and incentives — like "we need 100 assets this week, let's go" — with rewards for the crew that delivers. Fast, motivated editors earn more here, not just more hours. You only ever get paid for real work — and strong, committed editors consistently earn above their base. Learning & Growth — We Invest In You You do not need to be a branded-UGC master on day one. If you're coachable and hungry, we will get you there. We give you: •	Real examples of the content we want you to make •	Creators in our niche we admire, for inspiration •	Visual references for pacing, captions, and style •	A clear brief for every single asset In return, we ask for commitment. The training, the feedback, the systems — that's us investing in you. We're looking for an editor who will take that investment and build a long-term home here. Growth is expected. Perfection on day one is not. ________________________________________ How We Work (And Why People Stay) •	Work on your own time. We care about output and deadlines, not whether you're online 9-to-5. Start with the hours that fit your life and ramp up as you prove out and want more — part-time is a perfectly fine place to begin. •	A real community. Our team lives in ---------- — it's friendly, supportive, and genuinely fun. You're not editing alone in the dark; you've got a crew. •	Clarity over chaos. Documented workflows, organized files, clear expectations. You're never guessing what to do next. •	A system that has your back. For B-roll content, our system drafts a plan for each video — the building blocks come organized and ready, so you're never staring at a blank timeline wondering where to start. You get to focus on the craft. Tools You'll Use (We Teach You — No Stress If You're New) •	Google Drive — organized project folders • ---------- — feedback, revisions, approvals •	Airtable — a friendly editor dashboard where you track your work and pull each video's plan Every workflow is documented, intuitive, and built to be easy to follow. Never touched these before? We'll teach you. ________________________________________ About Us We build and grow creator brands and shoppable content across TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube — heavy on lifestyle, wellness, fitness, discipline, and the kind of content that makes women feel motivated and capable. Our content world: •	Lifestyle & wellness routines •	Fitness, discipline, habits, and consistency •	Creator education & behind-the-scenes business •	Affiliate marketing (Amazon, TikTok Shop) •	Brand partnerships, UGC-style deliverables, and paid ads There's a primary creator you'll edit for, but Creator Studio also produces and manages a wider library of content and assets — so there's always room to grow into more. ________________________________________ How to Apply (Follow This Carefully — It's Our First Test) 1.	Send 2–3 short-form samples 2.	Tell us: o	Your availability. o	Part-time or full-time o	Your preferred hourly rate o	Your experience with content creation/video editing 3.	In 2–3 sentences, tell us why you're fired up about this role. We read these. Two rules: •	Applications that don't follow these steps won't be reviewed. •	Include the word "seedling" somewhere in your message, so we know you read all the way to the end. If you've got the drive and you're ready to commit, we'd genuinely love to meet you. Let's workkk.

Spec work and personal projects count - Fast in CapCut, Premiere, or DaVinci — pick one, be quick in it - Vertical-first editing fluency (Reels/TikTok/Stories) - Fast turnaround — briefs Monday morning means first drafts Tuesday EOD - Coachable — you absorb feedback and apply it next round without getting defensive - Reliable async communicator — you don't go dark, you flag blockers early - Detail-oriented — you catch your own typos, audio glitches, and export issues before delivery ## Bonus (not required) - You've played with Higgsfield, Kling, Runway, Google Flow, Sora, or CapCut AI features — even as a hobby - You've used stock libraries before (Storyblocks, Pexels, Artgrid) - You watch a lot of ads and have opinions about them - Motion graphics basics (After Effects or CapCut templates) ## What this role is NOT - Not a creative strategist role — concepts come from us - Not a heavy AI generation role yet — you'll learn it over time - Not low-volume — expect 10+ variants a week once ramped ## Logistics - **Type:** Independent contractor, ongoing - **Compensation:** $250 USD/month - **Hours:** 20 hrs/week, flexible scheduling, some PST overlap preferred - **Location:** Remote, Philippines - **Tools:** We cover AI tool subscriptions and stock library access - **Growth:** Clear path to more volume, senior responsibilities, and higher pay as you prove out — strong performers move up fast ## How to apply Send all of the following — incomplete applications get skipped: 1. **Portfolio link** — Drive folder, Vimeo, or personal site. title: Total Video Editing Genius
description: The McCord List Media Network | Faith-Forward, Female-Founded, Nationally Syndicated ----- **Employment type: Starting at PT, but will quickly grow if this is the right fit **Hours:**  8-3pm PST ----- ## Read this part first We are not looking for someone who “does some editing.” We are looking for a total crusher. Someone who opens Premiere Pro and disappears into the work. Someone who turns raw footage into broadcast-ready episodes without being chased, watches the full cut before anyone has to ask, and treats a missed deadline like a personal offense. If you need hand-holding, this is not your role. If you have been waiting for a place that moves as fast as you do, keep reading. The McCord List Media Network is a nationally syndicated media operation reaching more than 90 million households across Roku, Amazon Prime, Samsung TV Plus, and Tubi. We produce The McCord List Today plus a growing roster of client shows, all from a real LED soundstage in Manhattan Beach. We are faith-led, purpose-driven, and obsessed with editorial polish. Every frame we publish carries the brand. This is a high-volume, high-standards seat. The right person will thrive on it. ----- ## What you will own You are the engine room of our content. Your job is to take raw footage and turn it into polished, on-brand, broadcast-ready episodes and the social clips that fuel our reach. Week to week, you will: - Pull and organize weekly raw footage from our Google Drive client folders by filming date, and confirm intro, outro, branding, and guest assets are in place before you cut - Edit full-length episodes in Adobe Premiere Pro: clean cuts, balanced audio, color and LUTs applied, awkward host ---------- nts and BTS removed, branded intro and outro graphics in place - Export final episodes in high resolution (both our 22-minute and 40 to 48 minute formats) and file them correctly under Final Episodes - Cut individual interview segments for each guest - Generate 30 to 35 social clips per episode in Opus Clip Pro, then review every clip for accuracy, brand tone, captions, logo, and framing before it ships - Maintain clean, standardized folder structure in Google Drive so nothing ever gets lost - Upload approved episodes to U Screen with complete, accurate metadata pulled from the Content Sheet (title, guests, description, SEO, category) - Keep the task sheet and dashboard current on every episode, and flag missing assets or technical issues immediately - Move episodes through our review chain: edit, submit to Nicole, apply notes, host review, final revisions, approved, posted - Jump on special projects when leadership calls: sizzle reels, highlight cuts, promo overlays, urgent social turnarounds ----- ## The numbers (this is the filter) We say crusher and we mean it. Here is the pace: - **8 to 10 episodes per week** combined across The McCord List Today and client shows - Roughly **3 episodes** for The McCord List Today and **7** for client shows - Every edit delivered within **24 to 48 hours** of raw footage delivery - **30 to 35 social clips** generated and reviewed per episode If those numbers excite you instead of scaring you, we should talk. ----- ## The quality bar We do not ship anything that does not look and sound like us. Every deliverable is checked against our QA standard before it goes out: - Clean, balanced audio throughout - Bumpers in place (first, middle, end) and the correct intro and outro sizzle - Names and titles spelled correctly - Nothing distracting in the background and no stray BTS left in - Correct brand logo, every time - Social clips with accurate captions, the brand logo, and the host or guest centered in frame - Consistent file naming: `Episode [#] - Guest Name - Final.mp4` You will be the last line of defense on quality. That is a responsibility we hand to people who take it seriously. ----- ## You are a fit if you - Live inside Adobe Premiere Pro and edit fast without sacrificing polish - Have a real eye for pacing, color, and audio, and you notice the small things other editors miss - Are fluent (or fast to learn) in Opus Clip, U Screen, Envato Elements, and Google Drive based workflows - Manage your own queue, hit deadlines without reminders, and communicate proactively when something is off - Understand brand consistency and protect it like it is your name on the export - Have published work for streaming, broadcast, or high-volume digital content (please send your reel) - Can troubleshoot audio issues and care about presenting work that crushes the game ## Bonus points if you - Have worked in a fast-paced media network, agency, or studio environment - Know your way around motion graphics and templated branded packages - Care about purpose-driven, faith-forward content and want your work to mean something ----- ## Why this seat You will be part of a media network that is scaling, not stalling. Your edits go out to tens of millions of households, not into a folder no one opens. You will work alongside a tight, driven team that values craft, speed, and faith. And you will see your fingerprints on a brand that is building something rare in this industry. We are looking for one person who wants to crush it here for the long run. ----- ## How to apply Send the following: 1. Your reel or a link to 2 to 3 recent full edits you are proud of 1. A short note on the highest volume you have ever sustained and how you kept quality high 1. The fastest you have ever turned a polished episode from raw footage No generic cover letters. Show us the work. ----- *The McCord List Media Network is a division of LaunchPreneur, Inc.*

description: We're Counter, a high-protein frozen food brand in the US. Our TikToks are real college students doing street interviews: handing strangers our food and filming their reactions. title: Premiere Pro Video Editor for Coaching, Training & Educational Content
job_title: Premiere Pro Video Editor for Coaching, Training & Educational Content
description: We are looking for a reliable, detail-focused video editor to join our team on a freelance/ongoing basis. We are a UK-based business coaching and training company that runs regular online and in-person events, workshops, coaching sessions and training programmes. We need an editor who can help us turn this content into clean, professional, easy-to-watch videos for our coaching platforms, member areas, YouTube, social media and internal training resources. This role is specifically for someone who has experience editing educational, coaching, training, webinar or course-style content. Please do not apply unless your portfolio includes examples of previously edited educational or coaching content. Applications without this type of portfolio evidence will not be considered. The main focus of this role will be editing long-form coaching, event and training content. However, we also repurpose our coaching content into shorter social media videos, reels and clips, so you may also be asked to edit short-form content from the same recordings. We need someone who understands how to edit content where the viewer is learning something, but who is also comfortable creating shorter, engaging clips for social media when required. The type of content you will edit includes: * Coaching session recordings * Online training sessions * Webinar-style videos * Event recordings * Workshop recordings * Course/member area content * Long-form educational videos * YouTube videos * Short social media clips taken from coaching or training content * Reels, vertical videos and repurposed clips Sometimes the recordings will already be captured through OBS and may only need trimming, cleaning up and exporting correctly. Other times, the edit will be more detailed and will require you to bring slides in and out when they are referenced, cut between speaker and slide view, remove unnecessary sections, tidy up pauses, improve flow and make the content easier for the viewer to follow. You must be confident working with long-form content and be able to use your judgement to make educational videos feel clear, professional and easy to watch. Your tasks may include: * Editing long-form coaching, training and event content * Trimming OBS recordings and preparing them for upload * Adding slides into the video when referenced by the speaker * Cutting between speaker footage, screen recordings and presentation slides * Removing long pauses, mistakes or unnecessary sections * Cleaning up audio where needed * Creating shorter clips, reels or social media videos from longer coaching content * Adding captions, subtitles, simple titles, lower thirds or branded elements where required * Exporting files in the correct formats for different platforms * Following clear briefs and feedback from our UK team * Keeping files organised and version-controlled * Communicating updates clearly through Slack Requirements You must have: * Proven experience editing educational, coaching, training, course or webinar-style content * A portfolio that clearly shows this type of work * Experience creating social media clips or reels from longer-form content * Expert-level skill in Adobe Premiere Pro * Strong attention to detail * Good understanding of pacing for long-form educational content * Ability to follow brand guidelines and editing instructions * Reliable communication and good written English * Ability to work independently and manage deadlines * A stable internet connection for downloading/uploading large video files * Willingness to communicate with our team through Slack * Willingness to use a verified time tracking app while working so hours and charges are accurate * Willingness to sign a contract protecting our intellectual property, client content and confidential materials Working Hours & Communication Our team works Monday to Friday, 9:00am to 5:30pm UK time. You must be available to work and communicate during these UK working hours so we can brief projects properly, answer questions, give feedback and keep work moving efficiently. This does not mean you will always be editing for the full working day, but you do need to be available during these hours when working on our projects. Clear communication is very important to us. We use Slack for day-to-day updates, questions, briefs and feedback. Important Portfolio Requirement Your application must include a portfolio with examples of coaching, training, webinar, course, tutorial or educational content you have edited before. If your portfolio only includes music videos, gaming videos, weddings, lifestyle edits or general social media content, this will not be enough for this role. We need to see that you understand how to edit content where the viewer is learning something and where the structure, slides, speaker delivery and clarity of the message are important. Bonus points if your portfolio also shows examples of short-form social media clips or reels created from longer educational, coaching or training content. Applications without relevant portfolio examples will not be reviewed. What We Offer * Regular freelance editing work for the right person * Clear briefs and structured feedback * Ongoing projects rather than one-off tasks * A friendly, supportive UK-based team * The opportunity to become a long-term part of our content production process * Interesting coaching and training content to work on * A mix of long-form editing and repurposed social media content We are looking for someone reliable, organised and experienced who can help us turn our coaching and event content into professional, easy-to-watch videos for our audience, while also helping us repurpose the best ---------- nts into strong social media content.

description: We're a fast-growing e-commerce brand in the health niche, focused on building high-converting video ads for Meta. We sell bamboo compression products — knee sleeves, ankle braces, gloves and socks — primarily targeting customers aged 50+ across European markets. Our flagship product, DailyCompress, is a breathable bamboo knee sleeve with one key difference: it's designed to be worn through the night. Here's why that matters. While you sleep, blood flow to the knee slows right down — so the joint stays stiff, swells, and never fully recovers, which is exactly why mornings feel so painful and stiff. DailyCompress applies gentle, even compression all night long to keep circulation going, flush out fluid and waste, and ease swelling and inflammation while you rest. You wake up with a more supple, less painful knee. On top of that: a perfect fit for every body and a sleeve that genuinely stays in place — for a group of people most braces were never designed for, and never designed to be worn in bed. What we're really after (please read this carefully) This is the most important part of the role, so we'll be direct about it. Our biggest growth opportunity sits at the very top of the funnel — with cold, "unaware" and "problem-aware" audiences. These are people who feel knee pain and stiffness every single day, but who don't yet know what's actually causing it, and who have often never been diagnosed with anything. By far, this is our largest audience. That means our ads can't open by shouting "arthritis." The ---------- nt we name a diagnosis, we shrink our reach to the small group that already self-identifies. Instead, our best-performing ads: - Lead with a felt symptom or a relatable everyday ---------- nt (that first stiff step out of bed) - Reframe the problem by revealing a hidden cause the viewer never connected the dots on - Then bridge naturally to the solution, the proof, and the offer So we are specifically looking for an editor who can build long-form, top-of-funnel storytelling ads that educate and reframe — not just conversion edits for warm traffic. Our videos are getting longer, not shorter. The ability to hold a cold viewer's attention for 2–4+ minutes is the single most valuable skill you can bring to this role. This is a senior role — we are not looking for a beginner. We need an experienced editor who has already made videos exactly like this and can prove it, not someone still learning the craft on the job. If you're early in your editing journey, this won't be the right fit, and that's completely okay. What you'll be doing - Edit long-form VSL ads (2–4+ minutes) designed to take cold, unaware/problem-aware audiences from "I have knee pain" all the way to purchase in a single watch - Build narrative arcs: hook ? problem ? reframe ? solution ? proof ? CTA - Edit with strong pacing for retention (cuts every 2–4 seconds, B-roll layering, captions, motion graphics) - Work with clear customer avatars and structured creative briefs - Translate written scripts and angles into emotionally engaging videos What this role is NOT We are not looking for someone who just "cuts clips together." We're looking for someone who understands: - why a 3-minute ad keeps a cold viewer watching all the way to the end - how to layer B-roll, text, and music to build narrative tension across a longer story - which 5 seconds matter most (the hook) and how to make them stop the scroll - how pacing, captions, and visual rhythm affect retention and conversion - how to edit differently for someone who is unaware of the cause versus someone who is ready to buy Requirements - Senior-level experience — you've already edited multiple long-form/VSL ads that have actually run on Meta. At least 3 realistic AI-generated scenes of older adults (50+) used for storytelling in video ads. 3. title: VIDEO EDITOR STANDARD — EMOTION & PERSUASION
description: VIDEO EDITOR STANDARD — EMOTION & PERSUASION Can be guys from Cinema school 1?? He understands that the script is NOT the final work A top-tier editor understands that: The script = intention The edit = emotional amplification His role is not to execute the script literally, but to amplify it visually by: proving what the script claims, reinforcing every message through imagery, creating emotion where words only suggest it. The edit must make the viewer feel what the script is saying. 2?? He can create emotion without showing the product This is non-negotiable. A strong editor can instinctively make the viewer feel something through editing alone. He knows how to use: Faces Gestures Situations Visual silence Micro- ---------- nts: eye contact breathing discomfort relief ?? He must be able to create an ad that generates emotion and desire even with no sound and no captions. If the message only works with text or audio, the edit is not good enough. 3?? He understands that pacing is a persuasion weapon A top editor uses rhythm as a psychological tool: 1–3 seconds max per shot (often less) Tempo variations to create tension and release Intentional pauses to let emotion land A great edit: is felt, not noticed holds attention without the viewer knowing why never feels “edited” ???? RED FLAGS (INSTANT DISQUALIFIERS) ? Script-execution mindset “I follow the script exactly” “I edit what’s written” Treats the script as the final output ? Needs product shots to create impact Asks immediately for product footage Can’t create emotion without showing the product Relies on features instead of feeling ? Text-dependent editing The ad only works with captions Overuses on-screen text to explain Emotion disappears when muted ? Flat or generic pacing Long shots with no tension Same rhythm from start to finish No sense of buildup or release ? “Pretty but empty” edits Clean transitions but no emotion Cinematic for the sake of style Focused on aesthetics, not persuasion ? Overused, stock-looking visuals Generic smiling people Obvious stock footage No real micro- ---------- nts or human imperfection ? Explains instead of making you feel Tries to inform before creating emotion Prioritizes clarity over impact No visceral reaction from the viewer ???? GOLDEN RULE (NON-NEGOTIABLE) If the ad doesn’t make you feel something and want to keep watching — and buying — even on mute, with no captions, it’s not a good ad.

description: Job Title: Virtual Assistant / Video Editor for TikTok Shop (Beginner Friendly) About the Role I am looking for a reliable and detail-oriented Virtual Assistant to help me with basic video editing for my TikTok Shop account. The tasks are super simple, and beginners are more than welcome to apply! I will provide the raw clips, and your job will be to make quick, basic edits to get them ready for posting. Responsibilities The two most important parts of this job are the following, and they should be your main focus with every video: 1. Cut out all dead space between clips. The videos need to be fast-paced and tight. Any pauses, gaps, or slow ---------- nts between clips must be removed so the viewer stays engaged from start to finish. Retention is everything on TikTok, and a well-paced edit is the number one priority. 2. Add plenty of overlays and photos throughout the video. You will be finding and inserting relevant images and overlays consistently throughout each video to keep the viewer visually stimulated and watching. The more engaging the visuals, the better. In addition to the above, you will also add a few brief onscreen text captions throughout the video to summarize key points. These do not need to be excessive — just enough to reinforce what is being said and help viewers who are watching without sound. Requirements The main technical requirement for this job is that you must have a smartphone capable of downloading and running TikTok Studio. All editing will be done using this specific app, which is completely free and very easy to use. No advanced editing experience is required, and beginners are absolutely fine! You just need to be willing to learn, follow simple instructions, and have a reliable internet connection to receive raw clips and upload the finished videos. Attention to detail is a must. To ensure you are reading this entire job post, at the subject of your application, put your favorite season of the year. If you do not have this, we will not consider you for this job. Pay & Schedule The pay rate for this position is $4.00 USD per hour, paid weekly. You will be required to keep a timesheet logging your hours worked each day, which will be used to calculate your weekly payment. In terms of workload, I typically produce between 4 and 9 videos per day. The editing tasks are intentionally simple, so you should be able to comfortably complete around 4 videos per hour. On a typical day, this means the work will take you roughly 1 to 2.5 hours to complete. Workflow Raw video clips will be shared with you through a shared Google Drive folder. You will download the clips, edit them using TikTok Studio on your phone, and then re-upload the finished videos back to the same Google Drive folder. No complicated file-sharing tools — just a simple, straightforward process. All edited videos must be returned within 24 hours of receiving the raw clips. For example, if I send you the clips on Monday, I need them back by Tuesday. This turnaround time is essential so I can maintain a consistent daily posting schedule. Growth Opportunity This is not just a one-off project — I am looking for someone to grow with long-term. As my TikTok Shop continues to scale, there will be opportunities for increased hours, additional responsibilities, and higher pay for the right person. If you are reliable, consistent, and take pride in your work, there is a real future here.

title: Editing Interior photos
description: Hello, I would love for you to edit these images as a test so we can see if we share the same style and vision before potentially working together on a long-term basis. The most important thing for me is that the images look natural and authentic. I shoot using natural light, and I want to preserve that feeling in the final result. The images should not look over-edited, overly bright, or as if they were lit with flash. These images are for a Christmas campaign, so I would like a warm, cozy, atmospheric winter feeling. I prefer a mood that is slightly darker and more cinematic rather than bright and airy, while still looking crisp, clean, and professional. Think Christmas, winter, hygge, warmth, elegance, and a premium feel. In particular, I would like: - Natural and tasteful enhancement of colors. - Beautiful and natural retouching of the model without looking retouched. - Natural-looking skin tones and facial features. - A harmonious and polished overall look. - Realistic snow and winter atmosphere outside the windows. - The outdoor winter scenery can be slightly soft or diffused rather than very sharp, so the focus remains on the interior and overall mood. - Removal of visible cables, wires, and other distracting elements when appropriate. - Removal of distracting reflections or other details that take attention away from the image. - A clean, refined, and visually pleasing result while maintaining realism. What matters most to me is the overall feeling and atmosphere of the image. I want the final result to feel genuine, premium, inviting, and believable—not artificial or heavily edited. If you feel that certain adjustments would improve the image, please feel free to use your professional judgment, as long as the final result remains natural and realistic. I look forward to seeing your interpretation of the images and hope this can be the start of a long-term collaboration. Thank you!

The feel is celebratory and energetic, driven by well-known upbeat pop music, with the cuts and speed ramps timed to the rhythm. Golden ---------- nts are kept in their original slow motion. The footage is shot on a Canon C400 (C-Log2 profile) and you apply a LUT we provide before any grading. We give you reference edits to match for pacing, structure and feel, so you are not starting from a blank page. It is edited in Premiere Pro, you hand back the Premiere project file, and review happens in ---------- with time-coded notes (one revision round on the trial). Beyond this first project, our work overall ranges from emotionally driven, story-led documentary pieces through to fast, energetic sport and event edits. WHAT THIS IS NOT. We are not looking for a generalist social-media editor. If your main experience is editing for YouTubers, Instagram, or short-form social (for example CapCut-style content), we are probably not the right fit. We don't do disposable, templated clips with tacky graphics, gimmicky sound effects, or AI-generated filler. We want a genuine video editor who specialises in considered, brief-led craft: emotional, story-led documentary work and cinematic, high-energy sport. Every piece is made to a specific brief, with real storytelling, craft and taste. TWO THINGS WE WEIGH HEAVILY (these are core to the role, not nice-to-haves): 1. A strong, fluent command of English, written and spoken. We will assess this on a short video call. 2. A genuine video editor specialising in craft work, shown in a real editing reel, not generalist, social-media, web or graphic-design work. YOU MUST HAVE (please be honest, this is where we have had trouble before): - A computer that can genuinely handle large-format Canon C400 footage (.mxf, C-Log2) in Premiere Pro, with a proxy workflow if needed. - Plenty of fast, free storage. Jobs are often 400GB or more. - A fast, reliable internet connection. You will be downloading large media and that download time is real. - Confidence with the ---------- Transfer app and the Google Drive app, and with relinking media in Premiere. - Premiere Pro, and you hand back the Premiere project file on delivery. - Comfortable applying a supplied LUT, working with slow motion and speed ramps, and cutting to music. - Organised and reliable, and comfortable communicating day to day on Google Chat or WhatsApp. - Able to take feedback through ---------- time-coded notes and action it properly. A BONUS (not a dealbreaker): After Effects and a sophisticated hand with visual effects. TO APPLY, please include: 1. Two or three of your most relevant samples as direct video links (for example Vimeo or an unlisted YouTube link), ideally matching our work: one story-led emotional edit and one high-energy sport edit. If you do not have directly relevant work, send your strongest pieces instead. Please do NOT send a full Google Drive folder with endless lists and subfolders for us to dig through; pick your best two or three and link them directly. It must be genuine video editing work. 2. Your computer specs and storage. 3. Your internet speed. 4. Your rate for a single project like this, and your monthly rate if we were ever to move to ongoing work. 5. References and proof of the work and credentials you mention. 6. One thing from this brief that stood out to you, in a sentence, so we know you have actually read it. We read every application and can tell a copy-paste from a real one. Applications that clearly ignore this brief, or whose work is not genuine video editing, will not be considered. A short video call is the next step so we can have a chat. THE DEAL. We start with this one paid trial project. If it works, we would love to keep working together on more projects and possibly an ongoing monthly arrangement later, but nothing is committed or locked in up front. Every editor we engage signs a short agreement: nothing you edit for us is used in their own promotion, and they do not approach our clients directly. This is standard on every job.

description: ABOUT SCRIVEINER LONDON Scriveiner is an award-winning British luxury brand specialising in writing instruments and premium accessories. Founded in 2019, our products are used by millions of customers worldwide, available via major online marketplaces and from more than 1,000 retail stores around the globe. Our mission is simple: to create beautiful, high-quality products that people love to use every day. The company has grown rapidly and has been recognised with numerous awards, including the King’s Award for Enterprise, The Sunday Times 100, the Great British Entrepreneur Awards, and multiple international design awards. We are high-growth, entrepreneurial and hands-on, and we are focused on delivering exceptional products and customer experiences. THE OPPORTUNITY At Scriveiner, design is not decoration. It is the product. From the curve of a pen to the layout of a product listing, every visual decision is an expression of what this brand stands for. Our customers have awarded us five product design awards. Our peers have recognised us with the King’s Award for Enterprise. The bar is not aspirational. It is already set. We are now hiring a Graphic Designer to own the visual output of the business: everything from Amazon A+ content and Shopify imagery to packaging, print materials, and retail partner assets. This is a broad, hands-on role with real creative ownership, not a production queue role where someone else makes the decisions and you execute. Scriveiner operates and sells globally, and as the brand expands into new markets and product categories, the volume and variety of design work will grow with it. If you want to build a genuine body of work at a brand people notice, this is where to do it. WHAT YOU WILL OWN Own the visual quality of every digital and physical asset Scriveiner ships: product listing images, A+ content, social graphics, packaging, print materials, and retail partner assets. Design and maintain product listing imagery for Shopify and Amazon, ensuring all assets meet platform specifications, convert effectively, and are unmistakably on-brand. Create Amazon A+ content modules including enhanced brand sections, comparison charts, and lifestyle image layouts that drive both conversion and brand perception. Produce and adapt assets for retail partners, interpreting co-branding briefs and working within third-party templates without compromising brand standards. Own packaging artwork from concept to print-ready files, coordinating with suppliers and production teams to ensure accurate, on-time delivery. Design product manuals, inserts, and printed materials to the same standard as the product itself: clear, precise, and on-brand. Build and maintain a library of reusable social templates across Instagram, Facebook , LinkedIn, and YouTube to enable faster, more consistent content production. Perform light retouching on product photography and provide simple video editing support as required. Maintain an organised, versioned asset library so all final files are accessible and correctly named. WHO YOU ARE Essential — you must have this A strong portfolio demonstrating ecommerce and product-focused design work. Amazon, Shopify, or D2C experience is expected. Proficiency in Adobe Creative Suite (Illustrator, Photoshop, InDesign) and Figma. A precise eye for detail and a genuine intolerance for off-brand, low-quality output. Ability to manage multiple briefs simultaneously, prioritise effectively, and hit deadlines without being chased. Experience designing for both digital screens and print or physical production, with an understanding of file preparation and production specs. Commercial awareness: you understand how design influences conversion and make decisions with that in mind, not just aesthetics. AI-literate and comfortable using tools to work more efficiently without compromising craft. Desirable — it would strengthen your application if you have Experience within a premium, lifestyle, gifting, or consumer goods brand where brand standards are non-negotiable. Familiarity with Amazon A+ content and product listing image best practices. Basic photo retouching and video editing skills using Adobe Lightroom, Premiere, or similar. Exposure to packaging design and working directly with print suppliers or production teams. Experience producing retail partner assets and adapting brand materials to third-party templates. WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE In this role, you will be successful when: Every product listing image and A+ module is visually compelling, accurate, and consistent with brand standards. Social and thumbnail assets are produced on time and require minimal revision. Packaging and manual artwork is delivered print-ready, with zero production errors. Retail partner asset requests are turned around quickly and to brief. The creative output of the business looks unmistakably like Scriveiner, everywhere. KEY WORKING RELATIONSHIPS Head of Marketing: your primary brief-giver. You translate their direction into finished visual assets and raise blockers early. Marketing & Ecommerce team: collaborate on asset requirements for campaigns, product launches, and retailer activations. Retail partners: receive and interpret co-branding briefs and partner asset requirements. External suppliers and print partners: manage file handover, proofing, and production sign-off. This is what we currently use and it works best for us — a different image model is fine as long as the quality is right. - Animate the shots in Kling (2.6 or Omni) from the keyframes, following the camera and motion direction. Kling currently gives us the best results for this type of video. - Keep the characters 100% on-model and consistent across all frames and shots - Use the assets I provide (story, song, scene structure, character reference sheets). - Edit the complete music video in DaVinci Resolve from the rough structure and scenes I send you. Videos are about 3–4 minutes long. - Cut the edit to the song. The song exists in English and German — you can edit to either version, the content is the same. - Send the finished DaVinci Resolve project back to us, together with all generated keyframes and animations. Requirements - Hands-on experience generating images with Nano Banana (Gemini) or a comparable AI image model with strong, consistent quality. - Hands-on experience animating with Kling (2.6 or Omni), or a very strong equivalent for this cartoon style. - Solid editing skills in DaVinci Resolve: cutting to music, pacing, rhythm and clean, well-organized timelines. - Strong eye for character consistency and detail — spotting and fixing deformations, extra limbs and design drift. - Understanding of basic cinematic shot language (wide, close-up, detail, dolly in/out, tracking). - Ability to follow detailed prompt templates and hard rules precisely (e.g. no human hands/arms on vehicles, no text in the image). - Fast internet connection and a reliable computer; access to (or willingness to subscribe to) the required AI tools. - Reliable, independent worker with clear communication. English is enough. Workload & Pay - We currently need about 4 videos per month. This may increase in the future. - From our experience, one video is doable in about 6 hours, so you should not need more than 8 hours per video. - Our proposal: $6/hour plus $52 for the AI credits per video — so about $100 per video. How to Apply Please reply with: - Your best AI video example that you made yourself (generation + edit), ideally character-based and consistent across multiple shots. - A short description of your workflow: which AI tools you use for images and animation, and how you edit. -  We'd prefer to agree on a fixed price per video. We pay you for 8 hours per video — no matter how long you actually need — plus $50 for the AI credits. (From our experience that's more than enough; we generally need quite a bit fewer credits.) Home Assignment (Test) You'll receive a short briefing with all assets and scene descriptions. Your task: produce the first 30 seconds of the song as a finished video. description: We are looking for a Freelance Performance Video Editor for e-commerce native ads and VSLs. We are building a direct-response e-commerce brand in the medical-adjacent mobility space. Our product is an EMS foot plate for people struggling with swollen legs, heavy legs, tight ankles, fluid retention, poor circulation feelings, and reduced mobility. This is not a beauty brand. This is not a fitness brand. This is not a generic wellness brand. We sell a specific product for a specific painful problem. Our audience is mainly older UK women who are tired of swollen legs, compression stockings, water tablets, heavy ankles, and feeling limited in daily life. We need someone who can turn validated native ad copy into strong short-form ads, short VSLs, and long-form VSLs. Important: This role starts on a freelance basis. Before we start paid work, we require one small unpaid sample edit. This is a qualification task. We want to see your editing style, thinking, B-roll selection, pacing, communication and ability to turn written copy into video. If the sample is strong, we are ready to move into paid freelance work. We pay fairly once we see that the skill, execution and communication match what we are looking for. What you will create: - Short-form video ads for Facebook , Instagram, TikTok and other paid ad platforms - Short VSLs - Long-form VSLs - Native-style video ads - Direct-response product videos - Problem/solution videos - Hook variations - Intro variations - Visual variations from already validated copy Your main responsibility: You will take validated native ad copy from us and turn it into strong videos. This means you must be able to: - Understand the sales argument - Understand the customer pain - Understand the emotional angle - Understand the product mechanism - Choose the right visuals - Source strong B-roll yourself - Build a video that keeps people watching - Make the video feel native, trustworthy and clear - Make the video support the copy instead of distracting from it You must be comfortable editing videos around topics like: - Swollen legs - Heavy legs - Tight ankles - Fluid retention - Poor circulation feelings - Compression stockings - Water tablets - Mobility problems - EMS foot stimulation - Calf muscle pump - Older customer demographics - At-home health devices The videos must feel trustworthy, native and clear. They should not feel fake, childish, overhyped or too “TikTok trendy.” Our audience needs trust, clarity, emotional relevance and a strong reason to keep watching. Must-have requirements: Please do not apply if you do not meet these requirements. - You have experience editing e-commerce performance ads - You have experience editing VSLs or direct-response videos - You understand hooks, pacing, retention and conversion - You can turn a written script into a complete video without needing every scene explained - You can source B-roll yourself - You understand how to visually support a sales message - You have strong English comprehension - You can work fast - You are reliable with deadlines - You communicate clearly - You can take feedback without ego - You have a strong portfolio with real examples A-player standard: We are only looking for someone who takes ownership. An A-player does not wait for every small instruction. An A-player thinks: “How can I make this hook stronger?” “How can I make the video feel more native?” “How can I make the viewer keep watching?” “How can I visually support this part of the copy?” “How can I make this VSL more trustworthy?” “How can I make this creative perform better?” If you only want to receive footage, cut clips together and wait for instructions, this role is not for you. We need someone who can think like a performance editor, not just a normal video editor. Compensation: This starts on a freelance basis. The first sample edit is unpaid and used to qualify the collaboration. If the sample is strong, we are willing to pay fairly for ongoing freelance work. At the beginning, compensation depends on experience, quality, speed and output. As trust, performance and responsibility grow, the pay can increase. Please send your expected rate for: 1. Short-form ad edit 2. VSL intro edit 3. Full VSL edit 4. Monthly freelance availability How to apply: Please send: 1. Your portfolio 2. Your best e-commerce video ad examples 3. Your best VSL or direct-response video examples 4. Your expected rate 5. Your availability per week 6. The tools you use 7. Your internet speed 8. A short Loom video explaining your editing process 9. A short answer to this question: “How would you turn a validated written native ad copy into a strong VSL?” Important application rule: Start your application with the word SCALPURA. If you do not start with this word, your application will not be reviewed. Unpaid sample edit: Shortlisted applicants will receive one small sample edit. We will give you one validated native ad copy. Your task is to create one short video sample from that copy. The sample should show: - Your hook editing - Your B-roll selection - Your pacing - Your captions/text overlays - Your ability to visually support the sales message - Your understanding of native-style performance ads This first sample edit is unpaid. Your sample is your first impression. In paid ads, the first seconds decide if people keep watching or scroll away. In this hiring process, your sample works the same way. Show us your best thinking, your best pacing, your best B-roll selection, and your ability to turn validated copy into a strong performance video. If your sample shows strong skill, good thinking, clear communication and strong execution, we will move into paid freelance work. We are looking for a long-term freelance partner, not a random one-time editor.

title: Faceless YouTube Tutorial Video Editor
description: ## Job Title Faceless YouTube Tutorial Video Editor — How-To Videos Based on Search Demand ## Job Description I’m looking for a reliable video editor to help create faceless tutorial videos for YouTube, Facebook , TikTok, and Instagram Reels. The videos will be based on “how-to” topics people are already searching for online. This is not limited to one category. Topics may include apps, websites, online tools, business setup, real estate websites, social media, AI tools, productivity tools, personal finance tools, home projects, and everyday step-by-step tutorials. The main goal is to create clean, helpful, advertiser-friendly tutorial videos that teach viewers how to solve a specific problem. These videos will not require anyone to be on camera. The editor will use screen recordings, stock footage, images, captions, text overlays, zoom-ins, arrows, callouts, music, and simple graphics. ## Main Type of Videos The focus is faceless “how-to” tutorial videos. Examples: * How to post a video on Facebook * How to use YouTube search to find video ideas * How to use Canva to create a thumbnail * How to use Google Sheets to track expenses * How to check if an LLC is active * How to use Redfin or Zillow * How to create a Facebook business page * How to use online tools step by step * How to complete simple online forms * How to use beginner software or websites The topic may change, but the format will stay the same: clear, step-by-step, beginner-friendly tutorials. ## Video Length Most videos will be **5–8 minutes** for YouTube. I may also need **30–60 second short-form versions** created from the same video for: * YouTube Shorts * TikTok * Facebook Reels * Instagram Reels ## Responsibilities You will be responsible for: * Editing faceless tutorial videos * Making screen recordings easy to follow * Adding captions/subtitles * Adding zoom-ins, arrows, highlights, circles, and callouts * Removing pauses, mistakes, and dead space * Adding clean text overlays * Adding background music and simple sound effects * Adding stock footage or images when helpful * Creating short-form versions for YouTube Shorts, TikTok, Facebook , and Instagram Reels * Creating longer YouTube versions when needed * Following instructions and making revisions ## Video Style I want the videos to be: * Clean * Simple * Professional * Beginner-friendly * Advertiser-friendly * Easy to follow * Not overly flashy * Not confusing * Not full of random effects The viewer should understand exactly what to do after watching the video. ## Important These videos need to be safe for advertisers. No profanity, no misleading claims, no clickbait scams, no copyrighted music, no shocking images, no aggressive hype, and no low-quality recycled content. I want useful tutorial videos that look trustworthy and professional. ## Required Skills Please apply only if you have experience with: * YouTube video editing * Screen recording tutorials * Captions/subtitles * Text overlays * Zoom-ins and highlights * CapCut, Adobe Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, Camtasia, or similar software * Good English understanding * Editing educational or tutorial-style videos ## Bonus Skills Helpful but not required: * YouTube Shorts editing * Canva * Thumbnail design * Motion graphics * Basic YouTube SEO * Finding stock footage * Editing AI/tool/software tutorials ## Application Instructions Please include: 1. Your video editing experience 2. Links to 3 tutorial-style videos you edited 3. What editing software you use 4. Whether you can edit screen recordings 5. Whether you can find stock footage and images 6. How many hours per week you are available 7. Your expected hourly rate or monthly salary 8. Put the word HOWTO at the top of your application so I know you read this post ## Test Task Before hiring, I may ask you to complete a short paid test video. The test will be a 30–60 second faceless tutorial video. I will provide the topic or instructions. You will edit it with captions, zoom-ins, arrows, highlights, music, and clean pacing. ## Pay Pay depends on experience. This can start part-time and may become long-term full-time work for the right person. ## Ideal Candidate The ideal candidate is reliable, detail-oriented, creative, and good at following instructions. I need someone who can take a simple “how-to” topic and turn it into a clean, useful video that people would actually watch.

description: Hiring: AI Content Operator — $15–25/hr, remote, contractor The setup . Taking the ideas and scripts that come out of our content pipeline and actually producing them — AI-generated, B-roll, whatever the format calls for. And repurposing what's already live into the next thing — same content, new platform, new cut. . Why I'm hiring That's the floor. The reason I'm posting this is I'm not handing off ideation — that part's staying with me and the pipeline I've already built. What I want is someone who can take a script and a hook and actually turn it into a finished, edited, posted, and repurposed piece of content without needing their hand held through it. Execution brain, every day. We'll still go through the analytics together — but production can't bottleneck on me. . Who we are I'm Vico Khang. I build and run AI automation and no-code agency systems on GoHighLevel — AI voice and chat agents, lead-gen automations, white-label SaaS — on real client accounts, not just talking about it on camera. The content side grew out of that: people kept asking how I was doing it, so I started filming it, and that turned into a real audience on Instagram and YouTube. We're not a media company that picked up automation as a topic. We're an automation business that happens to also make good content about it. Want the longer version, in my own words? Watch it here: ---------- . How to apply Fill out the doc here: ---------- . Day to day Building and maintaining the automations that move content from script to published post, cutting out manual busywork wherever it can. Generating the actual content with AI tools once a script or idea comes down the pipeline — B-roll voiceover pieces, AI-avatar or UGC-style videos, whatever the format calls for. Editing through AI tools first, and stepping in by hand only where AI can't get it there. Posting on schedule, automated where it makes sense, manual where it doesn't. Repurposing everything that goes out on YouTube or Instagram into TikTok, LinkedIn, and Facebook versions. Flagging anything in the calendar that needs a second look, and looping me in on the numbers — we go through those together. . What I need Real, hands-on fluency with Claude and the broader AI content stack — Gemini, Higgsfield, HeyGen — enough to take a script or idea and actually produce a finished piece with it. Comfortable building simple automations — Zapier, Make, n8n, or native tool workflows — so posting and repurposing don't need a human clicking every button. Solid editing instincts, and just as important, knowing which AI tool can do the edit for you and when it can't. Real, hands-on posting experience on YouTube and Instagram — you know the upload mechanics, scheduling, and formatting quirks of each platform cold. Comfortable repurposing long-form into short-form without needing a brief for every single cut. Decent English. We're filming for a US, UK, Canada, and Australia audience. . Bonus If you've actually run the production and distribution side of a channel — your own or someone else's — and know what breaks when you try to automate posting and repurposing, that's a big plus. . What won't work Someone who wants to own the ideation and strategy — that's staying with me and the content pipeline. And someone who needs a fresh brief for every single piece instead of running the system once it's handed to them. . title: Short-Form Video Editor
description: Purpose The Offshore Short-Form Video Editor turns raw footage from Paul Peterson and Alarmed Media LLC into high-retention, platform-ready short-form videos for TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, Facebook Reels, LinkedIn, and other assigned channels. This role requires technical editing skill, strong pacing, clean captions, emotional judgment, and the ability to make educational mental health content feel engaging, credible, and shareable without becoming gimmicky or misleading. Key Performance Indicators and Reporting - Complete 12–18 finished short-form videos per week during the initial phase, scaling toward 15–25 videos per week as assigned based on complexity and support. - Deliver first drafts within 24–48 hours after receiving usable raw footage and clear instructions. - Complete final revisions within 24 hours when feedback is clear and all source assets are available. - Maintain 90%+ approval within two revision rounds by following brand standards and instructions accurately. - Maintain at least 98?curacy for captions, spelling, grammar, platform formatting, export settings, and file names. - Produce correct platform versions, including 9:16 vertical exports and any assigned 1:1, 4:5, 16:9, thumbnail, or caption file formats. - Identify editing patterns, hooks, first-frame choices, caption styles, or pacing choices that may improve retention and report them weekly. - Use only approved, licensed, royalty-free, owned, or properly authorized music, images, video clips, graphics, fonts, templates, and AI-generated assets. - Maintain zero unauthorized use of client footage, PHI, testimonial material, OAC-restricted assets, copyrighted content, or unapproved third-party materials. - Organize raw files, project files, final exports, caption files, and archive folders according to approved naming and storage standards. - Upon achieving these key performance indicators, the supervisor will meet with the contractor to review progress and collaborate on establishing new performance goals that reflect continued growth, quality, and accountability. Core Competencies - Demonstrate strong short-form video editing skill, including pacing, captions, cuts, pattern interrupts, sound, first-frame quality, and retention editing. - Demonstrate the ability to preserve Paul’s message while improving clarity, energy, and watchability. - Demonstrate good taste and restraint with mental health content so edits feel credible, emotional, and professional rather than flashy or disrespectful. - Demonstrate strong file organization, version control, attention to detail, and ability to meet recurring deadlines. - Demonstrate appropriate escalation when footage, content, claims, privacy, or source materials create risk. Core Responsibilities – These duties may vary depending on project assignments and Company needs. - Edit raw footage into short-form videos, typically between 10 and 75 seconds unless otherwise assigned. - Create platform-ready versions for TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, Facebook Reels, LinkedIn, and other assigned channels. - Add accurate burned-in captions, clean text overlays, strong first frames, and visual emphasis that supports the message. - Remove dead space, unnecessary pauses, filler, repeated words, weak openings, and confusing sections while preserving accuracy. - Use zooms, cuts, b-roll, graphics, music, and pattern interrupts only when they strengthen the message and match the brand. - Repurpose long-form videos, interviews, podcasts, or presentations into short clips when assigned. - Recommend stronger openings, clip selections, titles, or visual structures when raw footage contains a better hook later in the recording. - Export and label all final files clearly by date, topic, platform, version, and approval status. - Maintain editing templates, caption presets, brand elements, file structures, and project files for reuse. - Communicate quickly when raw footage, audio, lighting, file access, instructions, or source materials are incomplete or unusable. - Perform other duties as assigned commensurate with the position duties. - Adhere to all Alarmed Media LLC policies, confidentiality rules, contractor agreements, and platform-access standards. Required Qualifications - 2+ years of short-form video editing experience preferred, especially with TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, Facebook Reels, or personal-brand content. - Experience editing educational, podcast, founder-led, coaching, health, mental health, or mission-driven content preferred. - Proficiency with CapCut, Adobe Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, Final Cut Pro, or comparable editing software required. - Strong English captioning, spelling, grammar, and on-screen text judgment required. - Ability to export clean vertical 9:16 video and adapt videos for multiple platform requirements. - Reliable computer, internet access, and secure file-management practices required. IMPORTANT: Please attach a link to your most updated resume and portfolio in your message.
